full_judgment:
3. Petitioner as Informant presented First Information Report with Nabinagar Police Station with allegations that accused Shahidul Islam and Ninety Four persons on forming unlawful assembly committed offence punishable under section 147/ 148/ 149/ 323/ 324/ 326/ 307/ 427/ 380 and 114 of Penal Code. The First Information Report was registered as Nabinagar Police Station Case No.15 dated 18.10.1998 which corresponds to G.R. No.241 of 1998. In the incident that took place on 18.10.1998 one Muktar Hossain was done to death. 

 5. First Opposite party of Revision Petition as Complainant filed a petition of Complaint before Magistrate, First Class, Brahmanbaria implicating the petitioner and other five persons. The petition of complaint has been numbered as Petition Case No.602 of 1998. 

 6. First Opposite party who is neither an accused nor a witness in G.R. No.241 of 1998 after submission of charge sheet against accused persons in the police case laid a Naraji Petition before Magistrate, First Class, Brahmanbaria. 

 8. First Opposite party, thereafter, moved before learned Sessions Judge, Brahmanbaria in a Revision petition under section 435 and 439A of The Code of Criminal Procedure (For Short the Code). The petition had been numbered as Criminal Motion No.73 of 1999. Learned Additional Sessions Judge, First Court, Brahmanbaria by a judgment and order dated 15.5.2000 allowed Criminal Motion, set aside the order recorded by Magistrate by which he rejected Naraji Petition and accepted charge sheet and directed Magistrate to proceed with the case in accordance with law. Learned Additional Sessions Judge took the view that first opposite party got the locus standi to prefer Naraji Petition. 

 12. Learned Advocate for petitioner has been confronted by this Court as to the maintainability of instant Criminal Revision Petition under Section 439 of the Code in as much as Second Revision Petition before High Court Division under section 439 of the Code stands barred in view of First Revision Petition before Sessions Judge under section 439A of the Code. Learned Advocate realised the legal predicament in maintaining instant Revision Petition and filed a petition for converting Revision Petition under section 439 of the Code into a Criminal Miscellaneous Case under section 561A of the Code. 

 13. Under section 561A of the Code, the High Court Division has inherent power to make such order or orders as may be necessary to give effect to any order under the Code or to prevent the abuse of the process of the court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice. This power is neither appellate power nor Revisional power and it is to be invoked for limited purposes. This power can be exercised to quash a proceeding where the facts alleged against an accused person do not disclose any offence. This power, also, can be exercised to knock down any conviction which has been based on no evidence. This power can be exercised when any order or decision is recorded without jurisdiction by any Court or Tribunal sub-ordinate to High Court Division. But it is, also, to be borne in mind that 561A of the Code does not confer unlimited jurisdiction upon the High Court Division and the alleged abuse of the process of the law or the ends of justice can only be secured in accordance with law including procedural law and not otherwise and the power is to be exercised in rarest of rare cases. 

 14. Judged by the touchstone of the above principles and keeping in account the nature of the decisions rendered by Additional Sessions Judge we convert the Revision Petition under Section 439 of the Code into a Criminal Miscellaneous Case under section 561A of the Code and treat the Revision case as Miscellaneous Case. 

 15. In the case in hand Police on completion of investigation laid Charge Sheet against accused persons and Magistrate accepted Charge Sheet on rejecting Naraji Petition submitted by First opposite party who is neither an accused nor a witness in the case. Since investigation stood concluded in submission of Charge Sheet, the same cannot be re-opened for reinvestigation. Re-investigation amounts to cancellation of charge sheet which is not sanctioned by any provision of law. In the event of submission of Final Report against accused person or persons, further investigation may be directed by Magistrate on the basis of a Naraji Petition either by Informant or any interested person. We are not acquainted with any provision of law under which a investigation culminating in submission of charge sheet can be processed for re-investigation and the charge sheet be cancelled. In State Vs. Abul Kashem 27 DLR HCD 342 it is observed : 

 "Further investigation may also be directed in a case in which some of the accused have been "challaned" i.e. sent-up for trial, and some have been left out, that is, final, report has been submitted in this case. And if the police, after making the "further investigation" submit charge-sheet against the remaining accused or any of them, then the report goes by the name of supplementary charge-sheet. A supplementary charge-sheet may also be submitted against an accused against whom a charge-sheet has already been submitted if further evidence has been available justifying his trial on an additional charge. All such subsequent charge-sheet are submitted on the basis of further investigations. Further investigation is not synonymous to reinvestigation. It is altogether different from re-investigation. Re-investigation, if permissible, will result in cancellation of the charge-sheet already submitted. There is no provision of law under which a charge-sheet once submitted can be cancelled. If the charge-sheet has been submitted by mistake, such as, against a wrong person, the proper remedy lies in withdrawal from the prosecution against him under section 494 of the Code. In fact there is no term like "re-investigation" in the Code and as such it should be given its ordinary dictionary meaning which is fresh investigation a course not contemplated in Chapter XIV of the Code, after submission of a charge-sheet." 

 16. First Opposite party in presenting Naraji Petition wanted re-investigation of the case on cancelling charge sheet submitted against accused persons. The course adopted by First opposite party is not at all permissible in law and Naraji Petition had been founded upon misconception of law. No person cannot be allowed to get his affairs settled in the way he likes and every access to justice must be misused as a licence to file misconceived petitions. 

 17. First Opposite party is neither an accused nor a witness in the Criminal Proceedings. Since the Naraji Petition is absolutely untenable and misconceived, the First opposite party, also, cannot be said to have any locus standi to maintain Naraji Petition. 

 18. Learned Magistrate on correct premises, accepted charge sheet on rejecting misconceived and untenable Naraji Petition. Learned Additional Sessions Judge appeared to have been blurred and obsessed by the submission advanced from the side of First opposite party and the impugned judgment suffer from patent illegality, legal infirmity and perversity and the same needs to be quashed. 

 19. Conclusion that legitimately flows is that converted Criminal Miscellaneous Case is allowed. Rule is, accordingly, made absolute. The judgment and order dated 15.5.2000 recorded by learned Additional Sessions Judge, First Court, Brahmanbaria in Criminal Motion No. 73 of 1999 springing out of G.R. No. 241 of 1998 is quashed. 

 20. Order of stay staying the operation of the impugned order dated 15.5.2000 passed by First Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Brahmanbaria in Criminal Motion No. 73 of 1999 stands vacated. The case will proceed in accordance with law.
